title: Generators & dynamos
examples: How does the speed of the magnet affect the electricity produced?
What is the difference between a generator and a battery?
Can you show me what the output graph looks like?

explain.say: Today we are learning about generators and dynamos. These machines create electricity using magnets and movement.

An alternating current or AC generator uses a coil inside a magnetic field. When the coil spins, it cuts the magnetic field lines. This cutting action causes an electric current to flow in the circuit.

items: Step 3: Current is induced in coil

draw.text: Coil spins, cuts field lines, current flows

explain.say: The current produced by an AC generator changes direction regularly. It goes up to a maximum and then back down to zero. This pattern is what makes it alternating current.
If you look at the output graph, the voltage follows a sine wave pattern. It starts at zero, rises to a positive maximum, and then falls to a negative maximum.
If you increase the speed of the coil spinning, the voltage output increases. A faster rotation means a larger rate of change of magnetic flux. This creates a stronger electrical current.
In everyday life, large generators are used at power stations. They convert the mechanical energy from steam or water into usable electrical energy for our homes.

faq.q: What is the difference between AC and DC electricity?
faq.a: DC electricity flows in only one direction, like from a battery. AC electricity, however, regularly changes direction, which is what generators produce.

faq.q: Does the magnet have to move for the generator to work?
faq.a: Yes, relative motion is needed. The magnetic field lines must be cut by the coil for the induction effect to happen. You can also move the coil through the field.
asks: Can I just put magnets near a coil?

faq.q: What causes the voltage to go up and down on the graph?
faq.a: The coil passes through its starting point, which is zero voltage. It builds up to a peak positive voltage, then passes through zero again to reach a peak negative voltage.
asks: Why is the graph a wave?
What happens at the zero crossings?

faq.q: Are dynamos and generators the same thing?
faq.a: They are often used interchangeably, but technically, a dynamo is a type of generator that produces direct current. Most large power generators produce AC.
asks: What is the difference between a dynamo and a generator?
Do they always produce the same type of electricity?

faq.q: If I spin the coil faster, what happens to the electricity?
faq.a: Spinning the coil faster increases the rate of change of magnetic flux. This results in a proportionally higher voltage output from the generator.
asks: How does speed affect the output?
Is the relationship between speed and voltage direct?

facts: Generators convert mechanical energy into electrical energy.
The principle used is electromagnetic induction.
AC generators produce current that continuously reverses direction.
The frequency of the AC output depends on the speed of rotation.

quiz.say: If the coil spins twice as fast, the voltage output will:
quiz.show: Double the speed $\rightarrow$ Double the voltage
quiz.why: The voltage produced is directly proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux, which is increased by faster spinning.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the rate of cutting the field lines is directly related to the speed.
wrong.1: This is too much of an increase; the relationship is linear, not squared.
wrong.2: This would imply the speed somehow reduced the efficiency of the magnetic field.

quiz.say: The graph of AC voltage over time is best described as a:
quiz.why: The voltage rises smoothly to a peak and falls smoothly back to zero, forming a characteristic sine wave pattern.

wrong.0: A square wave implies the voltage instantly jumps between levels, which does not happen smoothly.
wrong.1: A parabola suggests the voltage increases and then decreases symmetrically, but the wave pattern is different.
wrong.3: A straight line suggests the voltage is always increasing or always decreasing.

quiz.say: What energy conversion happens in a generator?
quiz.why: Generators take physical motion, or mechanical energy, and transform it into electrical energy.

wrong.0: This describes a thermoelectric generator, which uses temperature differences.
wrong.1: This describes a photovoltaic cell, which uses light energy.
wrong.3: This describes a battery, which uses chemical reactions, not movement.
